Reviewed in depth: parseFixed parses digit-wise and never touches parseFloat; products go through BigInt and narrow only via a safe-integer check so precision loss throws instead of silently truncating; rounding is half-away-from-zero and consistent across the parse and divide paths including negatives; proportion(c,h,h)===c exactly, so closing a position leaves no basis dust. The port owns recordId/recordType/clientTs/deleted structurally via spread order, del writes a tombstone, and records.js holds no Dexie import so the rules test under plain Node. Codex found three real bugs, all confirmed empirically before fixing: non-positive shares built a short with positive basis; unpadded MM-DD keys won the latest-close race as strings; toFixed rounds the binary value and lost a cent on 1.005. Accepted web/package.json ({type:module}) as a necessary deviation — Node 18.19 cannot import ESM from .js without it; flagged by the executor rather than buried.

Fee/tax divergence (fees capitalise into basis, taxes never do) confirmed as intended and promoted into ARCHITECTURE.md §4 in 335ef7f, since it changes every realized-gain number. FIFO/LIFO deferred with a ponytail: comment naming the upgrade path. 51/51 node --test at merge; 102/102 across both tracks on the merged tree.

Best call in this bead: the gain/loss accessibility requirement was implemented STRUCTURALLY, not as a convention. .wg-delta--gain/loss/flat::before emits the glyph from CSS and a test fails if it is removed, so a screens author cannot forget it and a future cleanup cannot silently delete it. Merged via PR #1 (branch b3-perf-engine). TTWROR + IRR in web/domain/perf.js; consumes portfolio.js snapshot({asOf}), never re-derives positions. 247/247 at merge.

Verified the headline claim independently rather than trusting it: ran my own bisection on Microsoft's XIRR example and the true root is 0.373362533519. The engine lands 1.9e-11 away; Excel's published 0.373362535 is 1.5e-09 away, and NPV at the published figure is -8.6e-6 versus ~zero at the engine's. The executor chased a 4e-9 discrepancy instead of widening the tolerance to make its test pass — the right instinct in a returns engine. Also checked the multi-root fixture algebraically: -1000x^2+2500x-1540 does factor at exactly 1.1 and 1.4.

Deviated from the bead deliberately and correctly: bracket-and-bisect with no Newton step. Newton's failure modes here all return confident wrong numbers and the repair for each is the bracket the fallback must build anyway — less code and no silent-garbage path. Non-convergence returns an explicit result carrying no 'value', so a caller cannot accidentally render a number.

TTWROR breaks at every flow day AND the day before it; that second boundary is what makes a mid-period deposit not move the result, and it is directly tested against the distorted 27.27% figure.

Codex: one finding dismissed after actually running it (excluding transfers as 'internal' prints a phantom -40%, because portfolio.js really does report the total dropping while a transfer is in flight) — both directions now regression tests. One finding fixed and real: same-day matched transfer legs applied gross diluted a 10% day to 9.09%; flows now net per day.

Merged via PR #2. web/domain/ppimport.js parses PP's .xml client file and CSV transaction export into §4 records, plus batches() for chunked writes. 256/256 at merge, CI green on go + node 18 + node 20.

Fixture provenance verified myself, since it is the load-bearing fact about this bead: the XML fixtures are byte-for-byte copies of PP's own test resources (portfolio-performance/portfolio @ 729a58e, file versions 63-69), attributed in THIRD-PARTY.md under EPL-1.0 with the upstream commit pinned. I scanned them for personal data before merging a public repo — synthetic accounts ('Konto', 'Depot 1'..'Depot 4'), well-known listed securities, no emails or IBANs. Not embedded in the binary (web/embed.go covers web/static only).

CSV fixtures are SYNTHETIC and that is the honest limitation of this bead — PP's CSV output is locale-dependent and needs a running app. Every behaviour is traced to a line of CSVExporter.java, but no byte of real PP CSV has been through this code. Filed as follow-up.

Two format facts the executor found that would have silently broken the importer: the .xml is an XStream graph whose top-level accounts/portfolios lists are often nothing but relative-XPath reference='../..' pointers into objects defined deep inside a cross-entry (without resolution the importer sees an empty portfolio); and a trade is serialised twice, once per side, both pointing at one buysell cross-entry, so that node is the dedupe key. sourceRows == imported + merged + skipped is asserted on both real fixtures.

Codex found three, all real, all fixed, none dismissed. The third was the executor's own and was exactly the failure this bead exists to prevent: PP's Delivery (Inbound/Outbound) had been folded in with cash transfers, producing transfer records carrying securityId — the shape §4 forbids, which portfolio.js silently drops while the report counted the row as imported. A silently dropped trade reported as success is the worst outcome available to an importer.

Four decisions escalated rather than guessed, all ruled and now pinned in ARCHITECTURE.md: recordId is opaque/stable with derived ids for imports (time+random ids make idempotency impossible); §5's lossless claim corrected — it does not extend to FX, which PP stores as BigDecimal; a negative amount is legal only on the cash-only types and is a data error elsewhere; assetClass is optional because PP has none and guessing one silently mis-buckets an allocation chart.

Merged via PR #3 (branch a3-a5-vault-server). Server: 002_vault.sql, store/vault.go, and internal/server/{rate_limit,session,webauthn,state,recovery}.go. Client: signup.js, unlock.js, ldk.js, vault-boot.js, vault.html. crypto.js untouched, as specified. All three CI jobs green.

Cold unlock is exactly one discoverable assertion as ARCHITECTURE.md §8.2 requires: login/begin returns no allowCredentials and login/finish answers {account_id, envelope} together. PRF is probed by an immediate get() on the new credential and aborts BEFORE finish, so a PRF-less authenticator leaves no account behind at all — better than the spec, which only required deleting the credential.

The finding that justified this bead's caution: the ported rate limiter was a COMPLETE NO-OP. Codex flagged it, the executor wrote a probe rather than reasoning about it, and one caller rotating X-Forwarded-For got 90 ceremonies through a limit of 30 — its own earlier smoke test had demonstrated the bypass and it had labelled it a feature. The sibling survives the same code only because it always runs behind Traefik; this binary is meant to be self-hosted and directly reachable, which is exactly the context a near-verbatim port drops. Now forwarded headers are trusted only from a configured trusted peer, defaulting to loopback. Deliberately NOT 'any private address' — with a published container port every request arrives from the Docker bridge gateway, which would re-open the bypass for every containerised deployment.

I verified that fix by mutation rather than trusting it: reintroducing 'trust any peer' reproduces the exact failure (90 through a limit of 30) and fails both named regression tests. The guard is real.

Two further codex findings, both real, both fixed: a failed recovery upload unwound to the welcome screen and would have minted a second same-device passkey (a named landmine, reached by a path the executor had not considered); and loopback IP literals were handed the https scheme.

Honest gaps carried forward: no real authenticator available, so the browser-side PRF probe, the PRF-less abort branch, signalUnknownCredential() and the kit download/print are unverified — ceremonies ARE driven end-to-end in-process with virtualwebauthn (real signatures, real discoverable assertion) plus a smoke run of the binary. Known degradation: srcdoc inherits the parent CSP so style-src 'self' blocks the kit's inline style, leaving the PRINTED kit unstyled (content intact, download fine) — correctly judged not worth loosening CSP on the page that holds the DEK. Deferred: no QR on the kit, no GET /api/envelopes (nothing needs it until A7), no envelope-MAC audit on unlock (a device-list concern, belongs to A7).

Merged via PR #4. index.html, manifest.json + icons, sw.js, features/{boot,screens}.js, the two guard tests moved here from B9, shell CSS, and a fix to fonts.css. CI green on all three jobs; 288 web tests on master after merge.

Verified against a real embedded binary rather than asserted: five slots navigate with hash, active pill, document.title and screen body moving together; deep-link reload lands correctly; self-hosted fonts genuinely apply (document.fonts reports Space Grotesk loaded, not a fallback); OFFLINE COLD START PAINTED IN 55ms with the network off, zero failed requests, reading real counts from IndexedDB — TRANSACTIONS 1 not 2, so the tombstone was honoured. CACHE_VERSION bump stages v2 in a separate cache while v1 keeps serving, prompts, and 'Later' changes nothing.

Found a real bug on master and fixed it: fonts.css referenced /static/fonts/... but embed.go roots the FS at web/static, so every glyph 404'd. Invisible because font-display: swap silently keeps the fallback — the app looked fine while shipping none of its own typography. I confirmed both the bug and the fix by curling the running binary.

Codex P1 was valid and the executor measured it rather than arguing: dismissing the update prompt does not pin the code — close every window and the staged worker activates without consent. It fixed the CLAIM rather than the mechanism, with the right reasoning: a worker that refuses to serve past an acceptedVersion does not bind the adversary §8 names, because the origin serves sw.js too. That correction has been promoted into README and ARCHITECTURE.md §8.

Deferred: no Lighthouse verdict (no Chrome UI available — installability inputs verified, not the badge), no real home-screen install or iOS Safari exercise, no in-app install affordance (belongs on Settings, g7e.7).

License texts vendored beside the components they cover: Dexie 3.2.7 (Apache-2.0), both OFL fonts, EPL-1.0 for the PP fixtures, and now Lucide (ISC) for the icon path data in wg-icons.js. Everything under web/static is compiled into the binary by go:embed, so a build IS a redistribution and both Apache-2.0 §4 and OFL require the text to travel with the work; the minified Dexie had its own header stripped, so that file is the only notice the artifact carries.

Lucide provenance was confirmed, not assumed — the chevron path data (m15 18-6-6 6-6, m9 18 6-6-6-6, m6 9 6 6 6-6) matches upstream verbatim. Header comment in wg-icons.js points at the text, since the paths live inside a source file rather than a standalone vendored asset.

architecture.vendor-licenses.test.js guards against drift in both directions (unregistered asset, and asset removed while left in the manifest); verified it bites on an unregistered file. THIRD-PARTY.md's 'Known compliance gap' section is gone because the gap is gone.

Closed by the same commit. architecture.asset-paths.test.js resolves every href/src/url() in every shipped .html and .css against the embedded tree, and separately names the /static/ prefix so the next author gets the reason rather than rediscovering it. Verified it bites by reintroducing the exact historical bug in design.html — 2 failures, then reverted clean. The rule is now written down in ARCHITECTURE.md §9 ('Assets are served from the root, not /static/'), which is the actual root cause: two independent authors made the same mistake because embed.go's rooting was never documented.

Worth noting why this needed a test rather than a review: neither historical failure was visible at runtime. font-display:swap silently kept the fallback font, so the app looked correct while shipping none of its own typography.

Merged via PR #5. state-sync.js (the §6 wire protocol, no storage) + vault-records.js (the §3 port). 353/353 on master after merge, Go green, CI green on all three jobs.

Verified the heart of the bead myself rather than trusting it: property-tested mergeRecords over 5000 random pairs — commutative across 738 collisions with EQUAL clientTs, idempotent, and a newer delete never loses. (My first run reported non-commutativity; my generator was wrong, not the code — it emitted duplicate recordIds within one side, which the Dexie keyPath makes impossible.)

The best judgment in this bead is the deterministic tiebreak. Without one, each device keeps its own side of a clientTs tie, a merge that changes nothing locally never schedules a push, and two devices sit on permanently different data with NOTHING to detect it. Comparing canonical forms picks the same winner on both sides for free. That is the failure mode most LWW implementations ship.

It also declined codex's suggested fix for the shared-metadata finding, with better reasoning than the suggestion: keying metadata by account would be WORSE, because localdb.js is one un-scoped Dexie database per origin, so a second account starting with clean versions on top of the first account's records converts a loud stop into a silent cross-vault upload. Instead the metadata carries its owning account and refuses a mismatch before touching the wire — and claims the mirror on OPEN rather than on first successful sync, because a vault used entirely offline never reaches the network, so a guard that waits for a response is absent exactly when it is needed.

Every load-bearing guarantee has a named test: rollback refusal, bounded retry then a real error, never drops a write, 401 distinguished from offline, tombstones retained, clock-skew correction, and the monotonic guard ('does not lose the edits of a device whose clock is ten minutes slow').

Honest gaps carried forward, all filed: nothing wires this up yet (A12), the mirror is not account-scoped (A13), and the metadata lives in its own IDB rather than §3's sync_meta because localdb.js was off-limits (recorded in the contract instead of pretending). Test files are split three ways to dodge a Node 18 runner wedge the executor could not narrow; documented at the top of the file so nobody merges them back. Not correctness — CI passes on both Node 18 and 20.

Folded into myportfolio-g7e.11 rather than run separately. Both change the same fold in portfolio.js, and sequencing them as two beads means restructuring the same code twice — the date validation and the CASH_SIGN export are now acceptance criteria on the restructure. Nothing is dropped.

Merged via PR #6 (branch g7e.7-screens). All five screens over the existing domain modules: dashboard, holdings, transactions CRUD, performance, settings with PP import/export. 19 files, ~3000 lines. 425/425 on master after merge, Go green, CI green on all three jobs.

The executor committed locally and then stopped WITHOUT pushing or opening a PR — the 'finished but unshipped' failure I had been watching for. I pushed it, opened the PR, and ran the codex pass it never got to. Worth noting for future waves: a local commit with no PR reads as 'no work done' from the branch list, and I nearly mistook it for lost work (the branch name was g7e.7-screens, not the worktree-derived name I was grepping for).

Verified structurally rather than by reading claims:
 - The money boundary is one-way AND enforced. forms.js imports only parseFixed/formatFixed (exact inverses) and deliberately does not import fmt.js, whose grouped '1,234.56' output is display text — parsing display text back into money is the bug that silently corrupts a portfolio. features.forms.test.js fails if any feature module imports toFloat; I confirmed the guard bites by adding the import ('not ok 1 - no feature module imports toFloat').
 - Position identity is opaque, per the mid-flight multi-account decision. Holdings renders from the engine's list and never keys by securityId, with a comment naming g7e.11, so re-keying by (accountId, securityId) turns one row into two without touching the file. The two position.securityId uses are actions (add a price, prefill a buy), not identity.
 - No hardcoded cost-basis label, so settings.costBasisMethod lands without a copy change.

Codex found two P2s, both confirmed in the code before fixing (8cb4a3f). The serious one was a CREDENTIAL LEAK: the API key field was populated once from the initially-active provider and never updated when the select changed, so switching provider and saving stored the old provider's key under the new one — the next fetch would send a Finnhub credential to Alpha Vantage. A password field hides that happening. The second: a successful import wrote its report to a slot importRecords() had already detached via refresh(), so the user saw nothing and would import again.

Merged via PR #8. Dockerfile (CGO_ENABLED=0 -> scratch, 5.3 MB, USER 65532), compose.yaml, .github/workflows/release.yml (new; ci.yml untouched), docs/DEPLOY.md, README section. CI green.

The acceptance criterion was DRIVEN, not reasoned about — real Traefik v3.6, isolated network, client containers on pinned IPs, limit 30/min: client A got 30x200 + 5x429 and spent its budget; client B on a different IP got its own 8/8; client C rotating forged X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP bought nothing. Crucially it has a NEGATIVE CONTROL: with loopback-only trust, client E gets 8/8 429 from client D's traffic. A test that cannot fail proves nothing, and this one can.

MYPORTFOLIO_TRUSTED_PROXIES is declared with compose's ${...:?}, so a stack missing it REFUSES TO DEPLOY rather than coming up quietly wrong. And compose publishes NO ports — load-bearing rather than tidy, because trusting the Traefik subnet is only honest while nothing outside that network can reach the app.

Two bugs found only by running it: COPY --from resets ownership to root regardless of the builder's chown, so first boot against an empty volume crash-looped on 'unable to open database file'; and Docker reused a freed container IP so the first 'client B' was literally client A — a false negative the executor caught and redid with pinned IPs rather than reporting as a pass.

Codex found three, all valid, all fixed. Two were P1 and both are supply-chain: (1) a push trigger runs ALONGSIDE CI rather than after it, so red master would still ship — now workflow_run on CI success, building head_sha (the tested commit, since github.sha on workflow_run is the default branch head at dispatch time); (2) workflow_run's branches: filter matches the TRIGGERING run's head branch, and ci.yml also runs on pull_request — so a fork PR from a branch named 'master' produced a successful CI run whose head_branch was master and reached a job holding contents:write + packages:write. Now gated on event=='push' AND head_repository==this repo. I verified that triple in the merged file; it is correct.

It also caught two errors in my own §10, both confirmed: the app never reads X-Forwarded-Proto (zero hits in internal/ and cmd/), and it already sets HSTS itself at internal/server/server.go:107, so listing it as an edge requirement invited two sources for one value. §10 corrected.

Not exercised, stated plainly in the docs and PR: a real Let's Encrypt cert, a full passkey ceremony (no browser), the GHCR push, the Portainer webhook.

Merged via PR #9. web/domain/quotes.js + tests, nothing else touched. 446/446 on master, CI green.

Provider: Twelve Data, chosen with a real reason rather than a coin flip — of §7's three candidates it is the only one whose free tier still serves daily history from the SAME endpoint as the latest close (/time_series), so 'current' and 'historical' are one code path with a days parameter instead of two that drift. Finnhub moved /stock/candle behind its paid tier; Alpha Vantage's 25 req/day with no batching would be exhausted by one refresh. Twelve Data also takes comma-separated symbols, so N holdings cost one round trip. A third provider is one table entry plus a load function — no adapter framework, as instructed.

Fixture provenance, which is the verification fact that matters here: CoinGecko market_chart and the Twelve Data single-symbol response + its 401 body were CAPTURED LIVE (verbatim values and timestamps). The Twelve Data MULTI-symbol envelope is written from the docs, because the public demo key rejects comma-separated symbols — the executor flagged that as the one shape a real key should re-verify rather than letting it pass as captured. It also ran the module end to end against both live APIs and confirmed both send access-control-allow-origin: *.

Privacy constraint held: I verified QUOTE_HOSTS is exported and frozen, both hosts are external and hardcoded, and nothing reaches our own origin. That export is exactly what 18h.9 needs for the CSP connect-src allowlist instead of restating hostnames.

Money boundary verified: the only Number() in the file is on an HTTP error code; prices go through parseFixed at a single conversion point. MM-DD chunk keys are zero-padded structurally — sliced from a validated ISO date, so the padding is guaranteed by the source format rather than by a padStart someone can delete.

Codex found three, all real, all fixed: one shared lastRequestAt let CoinGecko's request stall Twelve Data's first batch for a full 60s, freezing a mixed portfolio for a minute it did not owe; a per-symbol error in a multi-symbol response threw and discarded the whole batch, so one typo'd ticker cost seven good securities their prices; and a chunk-key construction that had disagreed between two sites, letting a PP-imported chunk be shadowed by a duplicate — now one helper.

Beyond the brief and correct: 401/403/429 halts that provider for the rest of the run rather than retrying into the user's quota, reported per security as bad_api_key/rate_limited. There is no retry anywhere in the module.

Merged via PR #10. THE LOOP IS CLOSED — the sync layer and the vault are no longer dead code. features/sync.js is the whole decision: it reads the warm LDK cache and either leaves localRecords in place or builds vaultRecords and hands it to the store. Nothing under web/domain/ changed, which is exactly what §3 exists for. 467/467 on master, Go green, CI green.

The load-bearing detail, and a genuine trap correctly avoided: store.js's records export is now a stable FAÇADE over a swappable impl. The domain factories capture the port object at module load, long before boot has decided anything — so reassigning the export would have left both engines pointing at localRecords forever. Dead sync that looks exactly like working software. I verified the façade shape in the merged file.

I verified the migration claim rather than trusting it, because 'my data vanished when I signed up' is unrecoverable: the test writes four rows including a tombstone through the REAL createLocalRecords, boots the vault over the SAME mirror, decrypts the server blob and asserts all four are present with the tombstone intact. VERIFIED BY THE ARCHITECT, NOT TAKEN ON REPORT
Four mutations run independently in a throwaway worktree, each confirmed red then reverted:
  drop a mid-span fx record -> "the EURUSD series must cover exactly the days the price chunks cover, in order"
  write a fractional rate -> the REAL engine's own malformed_fx issue, naming the record and the value: 'fx record needs { pair, date, rate } with rate a positive 1e8 integer; got {"rate":111862767.5}', plus the seed's integer guard
  declare the USD security EUR -> "expected exactly one non-EUR position, got []", "the fixture holds no USD position at all", "no transaction carries the §4 `fx` field"
  pin the rate to a constant -> "totals.marketValue 5386808 equals the naive native-currency sum, so no position was converted" and "the series does not move" — this is the assertion that actually proves conversion happens, and it binds.

The executor was honest about a limitation I would otherwise have had to find: with a rate for every day, deleting ONE fx record cannot make an engine gap, because fx.js carries the previous day's fixing forward by design. It therefore additionally holed the valuation day, which reds six tests with currency_not_converted. That is the right way to report a weak mutation rather than hide it.

COST, MEASURED
The fixture grew from 91 to 1928 records and from 199 KB to 481 KB of seed JSON; snapshot 27ms -> 31ms, performance 233ms -> 383ms (measured under node). Proportionate and inherent to §4's schema, which chunks `price` per security-year but specifies `fx` as one record per day. Acceptable for a demo; if it ever bites, chunking fx per year the way prices already are is the upgrade path, and it would be a §4 change rather than a demo change.

The assertions are on DIAL COUNT via a counting http.RoundTripper, not on the error text: 1 dial across two calls in each terminal case. 'Reports a nice message' would have passed on code that retries three times and then prints it.

Driven against the REAL relay handler from internal/server/mcp_relay.go rather than a fake, so it tests the protocol rather than someone's reading of it. All three failure modes — ErrPairingGone, ErrPairingReplaced, ErrDeviceOffline — asserted mutually exclusive by errors.Is AND by text with no substring overlap, each naming its own remedy. That mutual-exclusion assert is the point: conflating them is the actual bug, and this connector has now produced the unattributable 'looks alive, every call times out' symptom from three separate causes.

The executor's own honesty is worth recording: its first cut was RACY AND REINTRODUCED THE BUG IT FIXES — a Call's write can fail microseconds before readLoop reads the close frame carrying the code, so terminalErr saw no reason and redialed 3x into a 401. It flaked 3 of 5 runs. It fixed that in the CODE (awaitTerminal waits on the connection that actually failed, not on c.core which a concurrent Call may have replaced) rather than loosening the test, which is the tempting wrong move.

Mutation-checked: deleting the guard makes the terminal tests fail with the old 'gave up reconnecting after 3 attempts: ... got 401'.

Merged via PR #32. web/static/js/core/{mcp-responder,mcp-catalog}.js — the device leg, the Web-Lock election, mcp_help/mcp_call dispatch, and a hand-written read-only catalog. 704/704 web, Go green, CI green on all three jobs.

THE CHAIN IS NOW COMPLETE AND UNSIMULATED. mcp-shim-e2e.test.mjs builds and drives the REAL cmd/mcpshim binary over stdio -> real sealed frames -> this responder -> the real web/domain/ engines. Together with C2's TestTheRealShimBinaryReachesADeviceThroughThisRelay (same shim, real relay, Go stand-in responder), no leg of the chain is simulated on both sides at once — which is the property that makes either test worth running. The pipe here is a 70-line RFC 6455 server rather than the Go relay for a sound reason: the relay's device leg is session-cookie-authenticated, so reaching it from Node would mean replaying the whole passkey ceremony to prove what the relay's own suite already proves.

Read-only is STRUCTURAL, verified in the merged file: createRunner hands the domain factories { list } only, so no catalog operation can reach put/del even by accident. The single write in the file is the 4404 pairing purge, pinned by a test named 'the responder writes nothing but that one purge'.

The money boundary — the highest-risk detail in the bead — emits two fields per money value (authoritative decimal string plus the §5 scaled integer) and repeats the decision in each operation DESCRIPTION, because the description is the only part a model reads. A model shown 123456 with no scale will confidently report 123,456 euros.

The executor was killed TWICE by server-side 529s, the second time mid-fix on its third codex finding. I finished that fix. It closes the invariant the controller rests on — the lock is held IFF active is a live responder: 4409 already stepped aside, but 4404 purged and KEPT the lock, queueing every other tab behind a dead holder. Now unconditional rather than a branch that can be forgotten a third time (codex found it on 4409, then again on 4404).

I mutation-tested that fix and IT DID NOT BITE — the 4404 test asserted the purge but never the release, so the half that regressed was the half nobody checked. Added the assertion and confirmed it fails when the branch returns. Fourth instance in this repo of a test that passes on the broken code it was written for.

Deliberate omission with a reason rather than an oversight: the sibling's persistent anti-replay nonce ring is not ported. It exists to stop a relayed WRITE frame being replayed; every v1 operation is a query and a replayed query is idempotent, so it would cost an IndexedDB round trip per frame to protect nothing. It returns with the first write op.

Fixed on master directly — a one-line deadline change, cheaper than a bead. expectClose's 5s bound is a LIVENESS assertion, not a latency one: nothing measures how fast the close arrives, only that it does and carries the right code. Raised to 60s and verified 3/3 clean under two concurrent node --test runs, which is the load that broke it. It had cost me two false alarms while reviewing other branches.

Merged via PR #33. perf.js converts tx.amount through createFxRates at the transaction's OWN day and raises the same currency_not_converted issue when no fixing applies, so the two engines agree on what moved. 708/708, Go green, CI green. Only perf.js and perf.test.js changed; portfolio.js untouched, snapshot({asOf}) call shape unchanged, no time convention re-decided.

I verified the headline arithmetic independently rather than accepting it: reporting currency EUR, deposits of EUR1000 and USD1000 on a day when EUR1 = USD1.25, portfolio closing at EUR1800. Raw flows total 200000 and give a factor of 0.9000 — a portfolio that did NOTHING reporting a 10% loss. Converted flows total 180000 and give exactly 1.0000. That is the bug, in numbers.

Mutation-checked the load-bearing rule myself: swapping the lookup from the transaction's day to rangeTo (the newest available rate — the classic bug) reds 'a foreign flow converts at its own day before it nets against a converted valuation'. The test uses EUR1=USD1.25 in January against EUR1=USD2.00 in June, so a wrong DAY is a different number rather than a rounding difference, and it compares perf.js's flow total against portfolio.js's booked cash rather than a constant retyped from the fixture.

Codex found one real P3 and the fix is better than the report: an in-range transaction with an unknown type and a foreign currency raised currency_not_converted from perf.js while portfolio.js rejects the unknown type BEFORE its own FX lookup and never raises it — a fresh divergence between the two engines, pointing the user at FX data for a record both ignore. Gated on the record being classifiable as a flow at all, using Object.hasOwn so a transaction typed 'toString' is not read off the prototype as classifiable. That prototype detail was not asked for and is correct.

Codex's run also reported mcp-shim-e2e.test.mjs failing; that test spawns the real mcpshim binary and binds sockets, which its sandbox blocks. It imports nothing from this diff and passes locally both standalone and in the full suite. Not a finding.

Merged via PR #34. The Connect Claude card in settings.js — pure exported helpers (relayEndpoint/shimEnvLine/mintPairing/savePairing/revokePairing) plus a thin DOM layer, following the quote-provider card's shape rather than inventing another. 736/736, Go green, CI green. THE KEY NEVER TOUCHES THE SERVER, and it is structural rather than asserted: the mint request is sent BEFORE the key is generated, so there is no moment at which a key exists that the request could have carried. I mutation-tested it anyway, since a later reorder would break the argument — generating the key first and putting it in the body fails an entire describe block literally named 'Connect Claude — THE KEY NEVER TOUCHES THE SERVER', plus the real-binary acceptance test. The guard bites.

relay_url is minted with /api/mcp/relay on it and asserted against BOTH the pinned vector file and the actual route in server.go — not against a string the test and the code merely agree on. That is the contract that already 404'd C3 once.

Best evidence in the report: the responder dialled ws://.../api/mcp/relay/device?pairing=... and got 'HTTP Authentication failed' — NOT a CSP refusal and no path doubling. That is the §11 check-before-debugging item confirmed from the browser side.

Navigate-away decision, which I asked for and it made well: nothing is stored until the user confirms they saved the code, and minting drops the record for the pairing it replaced (the server keeps one per account, so that pairing is already dead). Abandoning the screen therefore leaves no device holding a key for a pairing that cannot answer, and the card honestly reads 'not connected'. Verified 0 rows at mcp_pairing between mint and Finish.

It declined codex's suggested fix with better reasoning than the suggestion: codex wanted the post-mint refreshResponder() awaited, but awaiting settles only once the Web Lock is GRANTED, so a tab queued behind another tab's responder would hang on 'Starting a pairing…' forever. The call was redundant (the relay 4409s the old leg at mint, and onStalePairing releases the election itself), so it was deleted and the count pinned at two.

One honest substitution: pairing_id is stubbed rather than minted through an authenticated POST, because Chrome's CDP virtual authenticator does not implement the WebAuthn PRF extension and the vault derives its KEK from PRF — real signup dead-ends on 'This passkey doesn't support PRF'. A browser capability gap, not a scripting shortcut.
